title: Authored Execution Flow contracts
objective: Let a planning agent and human author explicit Execution Flow trees, freeze them as deterministic SCORE data, show them in the Slice or Change Review, and deliver the unchanged expectations only to the File Agents that must preserve them.
requirements: A Change or Slice may contain zero or more named Execution Flows without changing the meaning of existing drafts that omit them.

Each Execution Flow stores a nonempty list of recipient target paths and a recursive tree whose root and every nested sibling group explicitly declare in_order or any_order semantics while preserving authored display order.
Each Execution Flow step contains nonempty plain-language text and may link to one Documented Declaration by its exact owner path and declaration name; unlinked steps remain valid.

Deterministic validation rejects duplicate flow names, duplicate or unknown recipients, empty sibling groups, invalid recipient paths, and declaration links that do not resolve to exactly one declaration owned by a file in the same Change or Slice.

Compilation stores each Execution Flow once as an immutable execution_flow Context Item, includes the exact authored flows in the shared Contract, and binds each item only to its named recipient Agent Briefs in authored flow order.

Each recipient Agent Input presents the complete unchanged Execution Flow as a required implementation expectation, while unrelated Agent Inputs omit it and retries receive identical digest-bound bytes.

Agent Input Markdown and canonical review HTML render the stored flow name, recipients, sibling-order semantics, nested steps, and resolvable declaration links deterministically, with a minimal semantic presentation that does not preempt the later review visual redesign.

Execution Flow content participates in draft, Accepted Specification, preparation, Contract, Context Item, Agent Input, and review identities so changing any flow creates the ordinary immutable Change or Slice revision while existing historical revisions remain unchanged.

Execution Flow is an authored implementation expectation, not an inferred call graph, runtime trace, verification result, status claim, or LLM-generated review summary; SCORE never derives it from repository or candidate code.
